title: Dimension reduction by random hyperplane tessellations
claim: Independent rotationally invariant hyperplanes give expected normalized Hamming distance equal to normalized spherical distance. Gaussian sign measurements can preserve distances uniformly when enough measurements are used.
mechanism: Map a unit feature vector x to sign(Ax), with independent standard Gaussian entries in A.
numbers: Theorem 1.5 uses m >= C delta^-6 w(K)^2 with probability at least 1 - 2 exp(-c delta^2 m). The finite-set discussion also explains a pairwise concentration and union-bound route.
threat_model: Mathematical embedding of fixed sets under random measurements; no image-watermark attack experiment.
limits: The unspecified constants and unmeasured mean width do not certify 128 bits for this project. A fixed pseudorandom public matrix, adaptively chosen images and correlated natural-image descriptors require separate empirical checks. The result does not justify the native Rademacher angular identity or a natural-image false-positive rate.
project_use: Prior art and theoretical motivation for a fixed larger Gaussian sketch; no novelty or security claim. Inspecting this paper does not select a projection seed or threshold from outcomes.
